subtopic: A power cut or rain spoils plans
subtype: Approach: waiting passively for things to return to normal [Pitfall]
passage: Urmila, stop sighing at the ceiling and listen. I am Anand, and when I was a boy of nine the lights went out across our lane for a whole evening. I sat on the sofa with my arms folded and said "I am bored" every few minutes. Nothing more. My sister was drawing by candle light, my cousin was drumming a rhythm on an upturned bucket, and Nani was telling stories, and I sat there like a stone, waiting for the fan to turn again. Three hours, Urmila, and I did none of it. When the lights came on I was more tired than if I had run around. And nobody had stopped me joining in.

qa.q: What did Anand say every few minutes during the power cut?
How was Anand feeling while sitting on the sofa with folded arms?
qa.a: Bored and cross, since Anand complained again and again and waited for the fan to turn.

qa.q: What could Anand have tried instead of waiting, and why?
qa.a: Anand could have joined the drawing or the drumming on the bucket, because the family activities were right there.

qa.q: How might Anand's sister and cousin have seen Anand sitting there?
qa.a: They may have wondered why Anand did not join, since they were busy having fun and nobody had stopped Anand.

grounding: A child sits doing nothing until the lights return, bored and complaining, though many activities were available.

subtopic: A power cut or rain spoils plans
subtype: Approach: waiting passively for things to return to normal [Pitfall]
passage: The power cut came on the hottest evening of May, and the inverter at Sonali's house had died the week before. Sonali lay on the cool floor tiles and announced, "I'm not moving till the power's back." Her cousin Pankaj offered cards. "No." Her mother suggested practising her poem aloud for tomorrow's recitation. "In the dark? No." Her grandfather started a story on the balcony, where there was a breeze, and Pankaj and the neighbour's children went out to listen. Sonali stayed on the floor, sweaty and cross, asking "How much longer?" every ten minutes. When the lights came on at ten, everyone else was laughing about the grandfather's ghost story, and Sonali still didn't know the second verse of her poem.

qa.q: What had happened to the inverter?
qa.a: It had died the week before.

qa.q: How was Sonali feeling on the floor?
qa.a: Bored, sweaty and cross, impatient for the lights.

qa.q: What else could Sonali have done during the cut?
qa.a: Practised her poem aloud or joined the story on the breezy balcony, both of which needed no power.

qa.q: What was the evening like for Pankaj?
qa.a: Pankaj went out to the balcony and enjoyed the grandfather's ghost story.

grounding: With the heat and no inverter, a child waits passively for the power, bored and complaining, ignoring the alternatives offered.

subtopic: A power cut or rain spoils plans
subtype: Approach: waiting passively for things to return to normal [Pitfall]
passage: On Saturday afternoon in their Lucknow flat, the power went, and so did the internet. Ayesha sat on the sofa staring at the black TV screen. "I'll wait," she said. Her brother Harish dragged out a box of old comics. Her father suggested finishing the jigsaw puzzle on the dining table. "It's too dark," she said, though the window was wide open and bright. Harish read three comics, laughing out loud. Her father fitted the whole sky of the puzzle. Ayesha kept pressing her dead tablet's button, as if it might come alive. At five the power came back and the TV came on. Ayesha had been bored for three hours and hadn't done a single thing.

qa.q: How many comics did Harish read?
How was Ayesha feeling during the three hours?
qa.a: Bored and restless, stuck waiting for the power.

qa.q: What else could Ayesha have tried?
qa.a: Joining the puzzle by the bright window or reading a comic with Harish.

qa.q: What was the afternoon like for her father?
qa.a: He enjoyed fitting the whole sky of the puzzle.

grounding: A child sits waiting for the power to return, bored for hours, while the rest of the family enjoys other activities.
